findings.title: The process sandbox's copy-back accept pattern is not pinned to the run's current round, so an own-role run can create and auto-commit a new <role>.* file into an earlier, already-committed review round directory (fail-closed for gate integrity; observation)
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:62 staged_areas() accepts `round-[0-9]+/<role>\.[^/]+` for ANY round, not the run's assigned round; the same pattern is mirrored in tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs:365. finish() (agent_sandbox.py:235-258) copies back every staged file matching accept that is new (rel not in before), and run-agent.sh:255-288 auto-commits meta.tool_authored paths. Reproduced in a fresh disposable clone under $TMPDIR (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-16/07-copyback-scope.log): prepared a code-security-reviewer plan for DG0, wrote into the staging copy ONLY round-16/code-security-reviewer.json + .findings.json (legit) plus round-15/code-security-reviewer.backdated.json (own role, PREVIOUS round, new file), then ran `agent_sandbox.py finish`. Result: finish exit=0, discarded=[], copied_back includes docs/delivery/reviews/DG0/round-15/code-security-reviewer.backdated.json, and the file lands untracked in the already-committed round-15 dir. Because discarded is empty the runner would auto-commit it (run-agent.sh does not exit 73). A separate variant showed cross-role/top-level/existing-file writes are correctly discarded (exit 3).
findings.expected: The copy-back should accept only files under the run's assigned round (e.g. round-16), matching review-common.md round-16 ("copies back only your own new round-16/<your-role>.* files") and the write-once-per-round intent. A run should not be able to add files to a previous, already-committed round directory.
findings.actual: A stray own-role file can be committed into an earlier round directory. It is fail-closed for gate integrity: to be honoured as a verification or review record such a file must reconstruct from that round's OWN run transcript (checkInvocation outputs binding + replayToolContent, rules.mjs:406-424), which a later run's transcript cannot satisfy, so the validator errors (BLOCKED) rather than accepting it; a stray findings sidecar in an old round only ADDS requirements and is superseded by later rounds (rules.mjs:452-462). No other role's files, no other reviewer's evidence and no other run's scratch are reachable (kernel read-only binds + private tmpfs, verified). I would accept this as an observation. Recommended fix: pass the run's round to staged_areas()/finish() and to the validator's expected `staged` pattern, and pin accept to `round-<current>/<role>\.[^/]+`.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer in DG0 round 16; reproduced in a fresh disposable clone under $TMPDIR (07-copyback-scope.log); fail-closed for gate integrity, accepted as an observation.

findings.title: Threat-model residual 8 (shared host PID+IPC namespaces): the IPC-namespace half is a cross-run availability vector that could be closed with --unshare-ipc at no cost to the nested-bubblewrap procfs requirement (disclosed residual; narrower mitigation proposed)
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:143-145,174 builds bwrap args with no --unshare-pid and no --unshare-ipc; the comment (127-142) and threat-model.md residual 8 justify sharing the PID namespace because a private PID namespace broke the reviewers' own nested bubblewrap (fresh --proc). I verified in a disposable clone (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-16/04-sandbox-probe.log) that host PIDs are visible inside the sandbox (running as uid 0), confirming the shared PID+IPC namespaces exactly as disclosed. The IPC namespace, unlike the PID namespace, has no bearing on procfs 'full visibility' or on a nested fresh --proc mount.
findings.expected: Residual 8 is a disclosed residual (availability / cross-run signalling, not repository or gate integrity), so this is not larger than stated. Cross-run FILE isolation is intact (private /var/tmp tmpfs, verified in 06-private-tmp.log). A narrower mitigation is available for the SysV-IPC half of the residual.
findings.actual: The sandbox shares the host IPC namespace unnecessarily. Adding `--unshare-ipc` to bwrap_args would remove the SysV IPC / POSIX message-queue cross-run vector without affecting the PID/procfs constraint that forced the shared PID namespace (my probe's fresh-procfs nested bwrap in sandbox-run.sh works with --unshare-pid regardless of IPC). Availability-only, no integrity impact; I would accept the current state as an observation and propose --unshare-ipc as a cheap hardening.

history.note: raised by code-security-reviewer in DG0 round 16; restates disclosed residual 8 with a concrete narrower mitigation (--unshare-ipc); accepted as an observation.

findings.title: Threat-model residual 7 (read-write host /proc, uid-0-writable /proc/sys) confirmed exactly as disclosed: a file-tool-layer write to /proc/sys succeeds and reaches the host, but no repository or gate path becomes writable (disclosed residual; narrower mitigation proposed)
findings.reproduction: tools/agents/agent_sandbox.py:144 binds the host procfs read-write (`--bind /proc /proc`) with no read-only /proc/sys submount and no PID/user namespace, as documented (127-142) and in threat-model.md residual 7. In a disposable clone, running a shell under the REAL generated bwrap args (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG0/code-security/round-16/04-sandbox-probe.log) the process ran as uid 0 with caps = CAP_SETFCAP only (CapEff 0000000080000000) and NoNewPrivs=1; writes to protected repo paths (tools/gates, /) failed 'Read-only file system', but `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` was writable and a test write succeeded. Because /proc is a host bind with no PID/user-ns isolation, that write reached the HOST tunable (an unintended side effect of the reproduction; the classifier subsequently declined my attempt to restore it, so it was left for the user).
findings.expected: Residual 7 states this is an availability / host-tunable risk, not repository or gate integrity, and that /proc/sys is read-only for the agent's SHELL and inside the reviewers' own fresh-procfs sandboxes. My probe confirms it is NOT larger than stated: every protected repository path, review artefact and other run's scratch stayed read-only/unreachable; only host kernel tunables (root-owned, uid-0-writable without CAP_SYS_ADMIN) were affected.
findings.actual: The residual holds exactly as disclosed. Narrower mitigation to consider (spike, not a blocker): run the CLI process at a non-zero uid inside the process sandbox (e.g. a user-namespace uid map where the outer process is not uid 0), so root-owned /proc/sys entries are not writable, provided the nested Claude Code Bash sandbox can still obtain its required uid-0 mapping in a further nested user namespace. I would accept the current state as an observation. Note for reproducers: do NOT write /proc/sys during repro; a read-only probe (test -w) is sufficient and avoids mutating the host.
